Lily wants to investigate the favourite gym equipment of members of her gym.

There are 700 adults and 50 children who are members of her gym.
Lily decides to sample 30 adults and 30 children.

Give one reason why this may **not** be an appropriate sample to choose.
questions.criteria:
1 point for a valid reason, e.g.: the sample is not proportional to the population — children are heavily over-represented (30 of 50 children but only 30 of 700 adults); or the sample does not fairly represent adults and children in the same proportion as the membership.
Accept any equivalent statement about the sample being unrepresentative/biased with respect to the adult:child proportions.

questions.prompt:
Lily decides to interview the members of her sample instead of giving them a questionnaire.

Write down one advantage of this method.
questions.criteria:
1 point for a valid advantage of an interview over a questionnaire, e.g.: questions can be explained/clarified; follow-up questions can be asked; higher response rate / everyone in the sample answers; answers are more likely to be complete or honest with the interviewer present.
Accept any equivalent sensible advantage.

importNotes: Source PDF has no cover page, so total marks and duration are not printed anywhere; totalPoints 50 is the sum of printed per-question marks and durationMinutes 120 comes from the '2h' in the source filename.
Tick-table/matching questions (11a, 12, 21, 25) were split into 0.5-point sub-questions to preserve printed totals; teacher may prefer whole-point weighting or recombining.

Numeric short answers marked by exact match (e.g. radius 21.7, 310000, 0.0390) may be entered with alternative rounding/formatting (21.71, '310 000', 0.039); AI near-miss checking should catch these but teacher review recommended.

Q13 (3D prism lengths) originally asked students to write answers on the drawing; adapted to two typed short answers (35 cm top length, 10 cm right height) - teacher should confirm the phrasing identifies the two blanks unambiguously.

No cover page in the extracted PDF (pages start at printed page 2), so no printed total marks, instructions, or duration; per-question marks sum to 50 and duration 120 min was taken from the source filename 'Grade 8-2h.pdf'.

Q11(a) matching (4 items, [2] total) was split into four 0.5-point multiple_choice questions; likewise Q12 (two tick-box statements, [1]), Q21 (two tick-box rows, [1]) and Q25 (word + number choice, [1]) were split into 0.5-point questions to preserve printed totals — fractional points need platform support.

Q13 ('write your answers on the drawing') adapted to two typed 1-point short answers; keys 35 cm and 10 cm derived from counting grid squares in the views (side/plan depth 5 squares = 25 cm, so 1 square = 5 cm) — worth double-checking against the original drawing.
Q10(b)(i) 'complete the sample space diagram' modeled as open_response with the partial table in the prompt; grader criteria list the full correct table.
Q23 [3 marks] and Q24 [4 marks] are answer-line-only questions modeled as short_answer, so method marks become all-or-nothing on auto-marking; teacher may want to review working manually.
Q17 answerKey is 21.7 (radius 136.4/(2π) = 21.707...); accept equivalent rounding such as 21.71.

Auto-cropped figures for Q4 (p02-fig1) and Q24 (p14-fig1/2) had dimension labels cut off, so full page renders page-02.png and page-14.png were attached instead; Q13 uses page-08.png for the same reason.
Q19/Q20(a)/Q22 each had two blanks under one printed mark of [2] and were split into two 1-point short answers each; Q14's table (two blanks, [2]) likewise.
